facts.statement: The type specimen of Owenodon was found in the Lulworth Formation of the Purbeck Limestone Group and dates to the middle Berriasian stage.
facts.quote: The first and only definitive specimen was found in the Lulworth Formation of the Purbeck Limestone Group, dating to the middle Berriasian stage.

facts.statement: Peter Galton established the genus Owenodon in 2009 after researchers questioned its placement in Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Peter Galton named the new genus Owenodon for it in 2009.

facts.statement: The fossil was presented to the Natural History Museum in London in December 1901 and assigned the specimen number NHMUK PV R 2998.
facts.quote: The specimen was presented by Hogg to the British Museum of Natural History (now the Natural History Museum) in December of 1901, where it was acquired and given the specimen number NHMUK PV R 2998.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Cherty Freshwater Beds of the middle Purbeck at Durlston Bay, dating to the middle Berriasian age within the Tirnovella occitana zone.
facts.quote: Owen's description of the specimens provenance suggests it was collected in the Cherty Freshwater Beds of the middle Purbeck where it was found in Durlston Bay, which is middle Berriasian in age as part of the Tirnovella occitana zone.

facts.statement: In 2002, David Norman and Paul Barrett reclassified the species as Camptosaurus hoggii based on similarities in tooth count and ridge structure.
facts.quote: Redescription of Iguanodon hoggii by British palaeontologists David B. Norman and Paul M. Barrett in 2002 found that I. hoggii was a species of Camptosaurus instead, creating the new combination Camptosaurus hoggii.

facts.statement: Kenneth Carpenter and Yvonne Wilson challenged the placement of the species in Camptosaurus in 2008, arguing it was more similar to Camptosaurus dispar than to the newly described Camptosaurus aphanoecetes.
facts.quote: The referral of Iguanodon hoggii to Camptosaurus was challenged by American palaeontologists Kenneth Carpenter and Yvonne Wilson in 2008, who described the new species Camptosaurus aphanoecetes and found it more similar to C. dispar than Camptosaurus hoggii was.

facts.statement: Greg Paul considered the species too incomplete to be placed in Camptosaurus and suggested it was an undiagnostic nomen dubium within Ornithopoda or Camptosauridae.
facts.quote: American palaeontologist Greg Paul also removed Iguanodon hoggii from Camptosaurus, as it was too incomplete. Paul recommended that I. hoggi was considered an undiagnostic nomen dubium, and an indeterminate species of Ornithopoda or Camptosauridae.

facts.statement: David Norman considered the separation of Owenodon into its own genus to be provisional, arguing the decision was based more on stratigraphy and geography than on anatomical differences.
facts.quote: Norman considered the taxonomic status of Owenodon to be provisional, with the separation of Owenodon as its own genus being a subjective decision based more on stratigraphy and geography than anatomy.

facts.statement: In 2012, Peter Galton expanded the geographic range of Owenodon by adding a tooth from the El Castellar Formation of Spain, while removing most Romanian material from the genus.
facts.quote: Galton also reviewed small ornithopods of England and Europe in 2012, removing the all the Romanian material except for maxillary and dentary teeth from Owenodon, but added a tooth from the Hauterivian to Barremian El Castellar Formation of Spain to Owenodon sp., expanding the geographic range of the genus.

facts.statement: The evolutionary position of Owenodon within ornithopod evolution remains uncertain due to the limited fossil material available for study.
facts.quote: The taxon, believed by Galton to be intermediate between Camptosaurus and Iguanodon, is of uncertain relationships, with the limited material preventing clear understanding of its position within ornithopod evolution.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Owenodon is a partial dentary discovered in Durlston Bay, Dorset, UK.
facts.quote: Conocidp a partir de un dentario parcial descubierto en la Bahia de Durlston, Dorset, Reino Unido.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, NHM R2998, comes from the Purbeck Limestone dated to the middle Berriasian.
facts.quote: El espécimen, NHM R2998, proveniente de la Caliza Purbeck, datada a mediados del Berriasiense.

facts.statement: Richard Owen first described the species in 1874, originally assigning it to Iguanodon as I. hoggii.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por primera vez por Richard Owen, que en 1874 lo asignó a Iguanodon como holotipo de una nueva especie I. hoggii.

facts.statement: The fossil bone was damaged during initial preparation but was freed from the surrounding rock matrix in 1975.
facts.quote: El hueso fue dañado durante la preparación inicial pero liberado de la matriz de roca circundante en 1975.

facts.statement: David Norman and Paul Barrett transferred the species to Camptosaurus in 2002, but Peter Galton established the genus Owenodon for it in 2009.
facts.quote: David Norman y Paul Barrett lo transfirieron posteriormente a Camptosaurus en 2002, pero esto fue refutado, y en 2009 Peter Galton asignó la especie a su propio género, Owenodon.

facts.statement: Owenodon lived approximately 143 million years ago during the Berriasian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 143 millones de años durante el Berriasiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Owenodon is classified within the family Iguanodontidae.

facts.statement: Galton interpreted Owenodon as a more derived iguanodontid than Camptosaurus but less derived than Lurdusaurus.
facts.quote: Galton lo interpreta como un iguanodóntido más derivado que Camptosaurus pero menos que Lurdusaurus.

facts.statement: Owenodon hoggii is considered a taxon with inconsistent and uncertain classification.
facts.quote: As its own species and genus, Owenodon hoggii is a taxon of inconsistent and uncertain classification

facts.statement: Analyses by McDonald et al. from 2010 to 2017 found Owenodon to be an early member of Ankylopollexia.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analyses of American palaeontologist Andrew T. McDonald and colleagues from 2010 to 2017 on have found Owenodon to be an early member of Ankylopollexia

facts.statement: Herne et al. (2019) found Owenodon further from Iguanodon than Camptosaurus, either unresolved between Ankylopollexia and Dryosauridae or closer to Ankylopollexia.
facts.quote: Alternatively, Owenodon was added to the analysis of Australian palaeontologist Matthew C. Herne and colleagues in 2019 where it was further from Iguanodon than Camptosaurus, either in an unresolved result between Ankylopollexia and Dryosauridae, or closer to Ankylopollexia.

facts.statement: The time range for Owenodon is recorded as Tithonian to Berriasian, from 149.2 to 137.05 million years ago.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Owenodon as Dryomorpha.
